hook: I'm afraid I'll be **arrested** in a case.
hook_q: How do I apply for anticipatory bail?

slides.title: Apply to the **High Court or Court of Session.**
slides.body: If you have reason to believe you may be arrested on an accusation of a non-bailable offence, you may apply to the High Court or the Court of Session for a direction.

slides.title: If granted: **bail on arrest.**
slides.body: The court may, if it thinks fit, direct that if you are arrested, you shall be released on bail.
slides.note: the court decides, if it thinks fit

slides.title: The court can add **conditions**, like:
list: Be available for police interrogation when required
No inducement, threat or promise to anyone who knows the facts
Don't leave India without the court's permission

slides.title: Arrested later? **Offer bail.**
slides.body: If an officer in charge of a police station later arrests you without warrant on that accusation, and you are ready to give bail, you shall be released on bail.

slides.title: If a Magistrate issues a warrant, it's **bailable.**
slides.body: If a Magistrate taking cognizance decides a warrant should issue first, it must be a bailable warrant, in line with the court's direction.

slides.title: Not available in **some rape cases.**
slides.body: Sec 482 doesn't apply to arrest on accusation under BNS Sec 65 (rape of a woman under 16, or under 12) and Sec 70(2) (gang rape of a woman under 18).

sources: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Section 482 (as quoted by the Supreme Court, State of A.P. v. N. Sanjay, 2025 INSC 973, sci.gov.in)
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 65, 70(2) (NCRB Sankalan, ncrb.mha.gov.in)
caption:
Worried you may be arrested? Here's how anticipatory bail works under the new law. 👇

1️⃣ If you fear arrest for a non-bailable offence, you may apply to the High Court or the Court of Session
2️⃣ If the court thinks fit, it can direct that you be released on bail if arrested
3️⃣ The court can add conditions, like being available for police interrogation and not leaving India without permission
4️⃣ If arrested later on that accusation and you're ready to give bail, you shall be released on bail
5️⃣ It doesn't apply to accusations under BNS Sec 65 or Sec 70(2) (certain rape cases involving minors)

Source: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 – Section 482; Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 – Sections 65, 70(2)
